votes.reasoning: The defect is fixed. Each Pending entry now stores a token. crossings() hands out tokens from `nextToken &+= 1` (NotificationService.swift:376-378), and every route that ends a delivery goes through isCurrent: delivered, park, and both the direct unmark and the authorizationStatus unmark (NotificationService.swift:187/193/200/203, tracker isCurrent at :340-342). After a reset, forget(key) drops the old entry. When the threshold is crossed again, it gets a fresh entry with a new token. So when the first add() completes late, its success, failure or park does nothing to the new crossing. rearmParked passes each entry's own token, so it still re-arms. No delivered mark is undone: unmark has an effect only if the token still matches the pending entry, and a confirmed or reset entry has already left pending. RACE-MAE-003 still works: a lower failure re-chains the higher entry's previous, and the token is left alone. The counter starts at 1 and is a UInt64 per tracker, all on the main actor. It would take 2^64 crossings to wrap, so tokens cannot collide or overflow in practice. Tests I ran: 41 passed on the fixed tree. I then reverted only isCurrent to `return true`, which matches HEAD semantics. That made 3 tests fail: stale_failure (3 vs 2), stale_success (2 vs 3), and unmark_stale_token. After restoring, the working-tree diff is byte-identical to reviews/diffs/B19-tail.diff.

No `try?` or catch was added and no error is swallowed; the failure path still logs through AppLog.lifecycle.error. The doc comments on Pending, nextToken and isCurrent explain why the token exists (RACE-MAE-004) rather than restating the code. The tests use expectTrue for the optional comparison (NotificationThresholdTrackerTests.swift:129), which follows the CLAUDE.md Boolean-guard rule. The report says the clean-build warning gate is at 0.
